title: Two elements of a Sigma type over propositions with the same first component are equal
author: The Univalent Foundations Program
work: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics
source_version: Homotopy Type Theory: Univalent Foundations of Mathematics source tree, file logic.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled lemma at source lines 467-470 (book Lemma 3.5.1): for a family of mere propositions, two elements of the Sigma type whose first components are equal are equal. The statement looks like a formality but the proof (source lines 471-475) has to invoke the path criterion for Sigma types, which turns the pair equality into the equation between the transported second component and the target component at the right point of the base, and then to notice that both sides of that equation live in one proposition of the family, which is where the hypothesis is used. The transport step and the choice of the point at which the equation is formulated are invisible in the statement.
